In nineteen sixty-two, a man lived alone in a cave, and lost an entire month.
Michel Siffre, twenty-three, climbed a hundred and thirty metres down into an ice cave in the Alps.
No watch. No sunlight. Just a tent, and a phone to the surface.
Every time he woke up, he called. Every time he ate, he called. Every time he slept, he called.
His team wrote it all down, and never told him the time.
He counted to a hundred and twenty, one number per second. It took him five minutes.
Then the phone rang. The experiment was over. It was September fourteenth.
Siffre thought it was August twentieth. He'd lost twenty-five days.
Alone, nothing marks the time. Every day is the same day.
Thirty-seven years later, he went back underground to welcome the year two thousand. He celebrated three days late.
